question.text: In the retirement stage, what is the MAXIMUM recommended allocation to growth assets?

explanation.text: The Logic: Once a client is in the income-drawdown phase, the primary objective shifts to stable income and capital preservation, while retaining a modest growth sleeve to combat inflation across a long retirement. A widely used heuristic caps growth-asset exposure around 25-30%, keeping the bulk of the corpus in income-generating, lower-volatility instruments. The Trap: Allocations of 40-50%, 50-60%, or 60-70% leave the retiree heavily exposed to equity drawdowns when withdrawals are being made, magnifying sequence-of-returns risk and undermining longevity of the corpus. Note: The specific 25-30% cap on growth-asset allocation in the retirement stage is not stated in the cited NISM Series XVII workbook pages, which mention a limited lower-risk equity exposure (e.g., not exceeding 20% for one bucket) but not this exact maximum. The framing above reflects general retirement-planning glide-path heuristics rather than a direct workbook citation.
